name: Amashsai
overview: Amashsai was a male priest from the tribe of Levi who lived in Jerusalem. He is noted specifically as the son of Azarel. His priestly role and residence in Jerusalem place him within the religious and communal life of the restored city during the post-exilic period.
namesAndTitles: The name Amashsai appears only once in Scripture without a recorded meaning or special title. It is a proper name mentioned in Nehemiah 11:13, with no indication that it was given by God or holds a particular symbolic significance.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture identifies Amashsai as the son of Azarel, establishing a direct paternal relationship. Beyond this, no additional family relationships are recorded in the biblical text concerning him.
scriptureSignificance: Amashsai's significance lies in his role as a Levite priest residing in Jerusalem at a time when the community was being reestablished after exile. His mention in Nehemiah highlights the continuity of priestly service and the importance of maintaining worship and religious order in the restored city. As a descendant of Azarel and a member of the Levitical priesthood, he represents the faithful remnant entrusted with sacred duties in God's covenant community.
